aggressive_definition: Fatal prostate cancer incidence in the entire initially cancer-free cohort
aggressive_definition_excerpt: Most importantly, only whole milk was consistently associated with higher incidence of fatal PCa in the entire cohort and higher PCa-specific mortality among cases.
study_design: Prospective cohort study with a separate survival analysis among incident prostate cancer cases
cohort_total_n_excerpt: We conducted a cohort study in the Physicians' Health Study (n = 21,660) and a survival analysis among the incident PCa cases (n = 2806).
reason: The abstract analyzes total prostate cancer incidence and fatal prostate cancer incidence in the entire cohort. It separately reports postdiagnosis progression to fatal disease, which is a survival endpoint and is not treated as incidence.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: The intake of total dairy products was associated with increased PCa incidence [HR = 1.12 (95% CI: 0.93, 1.35); >2.5 servings/d vs. ≤0.5 servings/d].
estimate_classifications.reason: This row is explicitly for total prostate cancer incidence and must not be relabeled as aggressive merely because the article also analyzes fatal incidence.

additional_estimates.comparison: ≥237 mL/d (1 serving/d) of whole milk vs. rarely consumed
additional_estimates.effect_excerpt: Skim/low-fat milk intake was positively associated with risk of low-grade, early stage, and screen-detected cancers, whereas whole milk intake was associated only with fatal PCa [HR = 1.49 (95% CI: 0.97, 2.28); ≥237 mL/d (1 serving/d) vs. rarely consumed].
additional_estimates.count_excerpt: PCa cases and deaths (n = 305) were confirmed during follow-up.
additional_estimates.endpoint_definition: Fatal prostate cancer incidence in the entire cohort
